page.layout: One page of text with a woodcut ornament and historiated initial; line numbers printed in the right margin (10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40) beside the text; no left margin text. Top: page number above the ornament. Then title block (centred), then body text, then a second section headed PROLOGVS LIBRI II, ending with catchword PRO- at the foot.

main_text.l: LIBER HISTORIARVM PHILIPPICARVM,
ET TOTIVS MVNDI
origines, & terræ
situs.
PRIMO volumine continentur hæc,
Imperium Assyriorum à Nino rege,
vsque ad Sardanapalum. Post quem
translatum est per Arbactum ad Me-
dos, vsq; ad vltimum regem Astiagen.
Is à nepote suo Cyro pulsus regno: &
Persæ regno potiti. Vt Croeso Lydiæ regi bellum intulit
Cyrus; victumque cepit. Hic in excessu dicti Æolicarum
& Ionicarum vrbium situs; originesque Lydorum, & in
Italia Tuscorum. Post Cyrum, filius Cambyses Ægy-
ptum in domuit. Repetitæ Ægypti origines vrbium. Extinc-
to Cambyse, Darius occisis Magis regnum Persicum ac-
cepit; captaque Babylone, bella Scythica molitus est.
PROLOGVS LIBRI II.
SEcundo volumine continentur hæc; Scythiæ & Ponti
situs; originesque Scythiæ, vsque ad bellum quo est in-
de pulsus Darius: qui post hanc fugam Græciæ bellum in-
tulit, per Datin & Tisafernem, quod soli Athenienses te-
nuere. Hic origines Athenarum repetitæ, & reges vsque
ad Pisistrati tyrannidem, qua extincta vicere Persas. Vt,
mortuo Dario filius Xerxes bellum Græciæ intulit: ac re-
petitæ origines Thessaliæ: expulsoque Græcia Xerxe
bellum ab Athenienfibus translatum in Asiam, vsque ad
Xerxis interitum.
PRO-

page.notes: Woodcut ornament at top and historiated initial D; the printed page number 310 is at the head. Right-margin line numbers 10–40 are marginal line markers. Some words in the body are faint or show-through; "Croeso" read as Crœso and "Datin" as Datis are uncertain; "Ægyptum in domuit" likely "in domum". Catchword PRO- at foot.
